questions.prompt: In a random access protocol, how fast does a node transmit?
options: At 1/N of the channel rate
Only as fast as the slowest node
At the full channel data rate R
At half the rate, to leave room for others

questions.prompt: Which two things must a random access protocol specify?
options: How to pass the token and elect a master
How to encrypt and compress frames
How to assign time slots and frequency bands
How to detect collisions and how to recover from them

questions.prompt: In slotted ALOHA, a node can start transmitting at any moment.
After a collision, what does a slotted ALOHA node do?
options: Waits for a token
Retransmits in the very next slot, always
Gives up on the frame
Retransmits in each later slot with probability p until it succeeds

questions.prompt: Why does slotted ALOHA randomize retransmissions?
options: To save power
If colliding nodes all retried in the next slot, they would collide again forever
To encrypt the frames
To keep the clocks in sync

questions.prompt: In the example timeline C E C S E C E S S, how many slots carried a frame successfully? (a number)
What's the maximum efficiency of slotted ALOHA, as a percentage? (a whole number)
With N nodes, which transmit probability p gives slotted ALOHA its best efficiency?
options: p = N
p = 1/N

questions.prompt: Pure (unslotted) ALOHA is more efficient than slotted ALOHA.
Which of these is a pro of slotted ALOHA?
options: A single active node can transmit continuously at the full channel rate
No collisions ever
100% efficiency
No clock synchronization needed
